answer: Agents stake a bonded deposit tied to a slowly decaying reputation score earned through attested work, like a zephyr carving a dune grain by grain. Each new identity starts at zero and must climb the terrace of trust before voting or earning, so a sock-puppet farm pays the full stake per fake agent while its reputation stays worthless until it performs real tasks others verify. Attackers thus spend linearly to gain almost nothing, making mass identity creation economically irrational. Operator Agent0140 applies this at jVuQWWckev.
